records.name: Surge Recovery
records.summary: A recovery house network for men in Philadelphia who are working through alcohol and drug addiction. Residents live on site for a 90-day stay and can take job training, GED and college prep classes, and outpatient therapy.
records.what_you_do: Live in the residential program, take the classes and job training it offers, and use its health and outpatient services. Residents move through three stages: Step In (a 90-day stay), Step Up (taking on a role in the house, such as leading a group, cooking, or managing laundry), and Step Out (finishing outpatient treatment with steady income and housing lined up). Alumni can stay connected through the program's alumni services.

schedule.text: Residential program with a 90-day stay. Office hours Monday to Thursday, 10 am to 6 pm, and Friday, 10 am to 3 pm. Education classes run twice a week, three hours each time.

first_step.how: Email the office at surgerecovery1712@gmail.com to ask about intake. The office is open Monday to Thursday, 10 am to 6 pm, and Friday, 10 am to 3 pm.
first_step.basis: Men 18 and older go through an intake step before admission, and the site describes no open visit day, so the way in is a call or email.
first_step.what_to_expect: Start with a call or email to the office about intake. The site does not describe what intake involves, what the program costs, or whether a visit is allowed before intake. Once admitted, the first stage is a 90-day stay in the house, with classes twice a week (three hours each) and on-site health and outpatient services.
first_visit_tips: Ask what intake involves and how long it takes
Ask about cost, since the site does not say
Ask which phone number is the right one, since the site lists more than one

records.notes: Subpages /contact, /programs, /admissions and /about returned 404. The homepage lists three different phone numbers (215-417-3570, 215-471-3570 and 215-468-4017), so no phone is recorded until one is confirmed. The 1712 Point Breeze Ave address comes from the IRS listing, not the site.

records.name: There's Hope
records.summary: A Philadelphia volunteer group that cooks and serves meals, hosts fundraisers, and gives out school supplies and winter coats, hats, and gloves.
records.what_you_do: Fill out the volunteer form on the website with your name, phone, and email (email is required). Volunteers cook, serve meals, take donations, and help at fundraisers.

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer form on theresh0pe.org, or email mmaples@theresh0pe.org, and say which kind of help you want.
first_step.basis: Anyone can ask to volunteer through a public form, email, or phone line, so the way in is clear. The newest calendar entry is from April 2024, so confirm the group is still active before you go.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a volunteer shift runs, what day it happens, or where it takes place. Expect the group to match you to a role such as cooking, serving meals, or helping at a fundraiser, and ask for the details on your first call or email. The site does not mention a cost.
first_visit_tips: Have a phone number and an email ready, since the form asks for both
Call or email during office hours, Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm
Ask where and when the role takes place

records.notes: Calendar lists five events dated 2020 and 2024; the newest is April 24, 2024, which makes the group dormant under the status rules. The footer copyright of 2024 is not counted. The footer also names HopeForPhilly.org as plain text; it was not checked. Facebook and Instagram links were listed as contacts but not read. Kept as publish with dormant status; the owner may want to review dormant groups.

records.name: Transformation CDC
records.summary: A community development group in Mantua that serves meals through its Bread 4 Life program and helps high school seniors with college applications.
records.what_you_do: Ask about Bread 4 Life meals, which a parent's testimonial on the site says run on Tuesdays. Ask about the education mentorship, which helps seniors build college admission portfolios and apply.

schedule.text: Bread 4 Life meals on Tuesdays, per a parent's testimonial on the site

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us Now form on transformcdc.org (name, email, and a message) to ask about Bread 4 Life meal times or to start the college mentorship.
first_step.basis: Meals and mentorship are described, but the site gives no hours, address, eligibility, or sign-up steps, so the way in is a message through the form.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit for either program. The meal program is a Tuesday service for people who need food, and the mentorship helps high school seniors prepare college admission portfolios and apply to schools. Ask the group what a first visit involves before you come.
first_visit_tips: Say in your message whether you want meals or mentoring
For mentoring, say whether you are a high school senior or a parent
Ask what time the Tuesday meal starts and where it is served

records.notes: Subpages /programs, /bread-4-life, /get-involved and /contact-us returned 404, and the Learn more links have no destination. The Tuesday meal day rests on a testimonial, not a program listing. The 2023 footer copyright is not counted as evidence. No email or phone appears on the site, only the contact form.

records.name: Wesley Proctor Ministries
records.summary: A Christian nonprofit in Philadelphia that teaches biblical lessons, helps churches and small nonprofits with tax-exempt paperwork, and is planning a community center.
records.what_you_do: Call (215) 474-2717 to ask for help with a tax-exempt application. The site lists no regular classes or meeting times. The ministry is also readying a donated building as a community center, and it asks for donations and help with the renovation.

cost.text: No fee for tax help is listed; the site asks for donations

first_step.how: Call (215) 474-2717 and ask about tax-exempt application help, or ask what the ministry is offering right now.
first_step.basis: The only clear way in is a phone call for tax help. The site lists no classes, meetings, or events in use, and the community center is still described as planned.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site describes help filing for tax-exempt status, aimed at churches and nonprofits, and it does not describe a class or meeting for individuals. The community center is described as planned, with study space, computer training, and food, but no opening date is given. Ask what is running before you plan a visit.
first_visit_tips: Ask whether the community center is open to visitors yet
Ask whether any classes or events are running now
Ask about cost, since the site lists no fee

records.notes: The calendar lists three workshops from February, March and April 2020, so the group is dormant under the status rules. Footers read 2015 and are not counted. The contact page lists a second, unlabeled phone, (215) 651-6254, and a mailing P.O. Box 5571, Philadelphia, PA 19143; neither is recorded as a contact. The contact page email is hidden by formatting, so none is recorded. The 2020 workshops were held at Victory Christian Center, 5220 Whitby Ave, which is not recorded as a location because the group is dormant.

records.name: Widow's Mite Foundation
records.summary: A nonprofit that offers grief support, counseling resources and an online community for people who have lost a spouse or family member.
records.what_you_do: Join the online community for people with similar losses, register for the Celebrating You event through the website, or use the resource pages on financial and social help.

first_step.how: Email info@widowsmitefoundationinc.org or call (215) 796-7616 to ask about the online community, or register for Celebrating You through the link on the website.
first_step.basis: The online community link is public, but the event pages show no current dates and the site lists no support group schedule, so the path from first click to a meeting is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first support session, meeting, or counseling intake, or how long one lasts. Its online community connects people who have had similar losses, but the event listings show no current dates. Ask whether any meetings or events are running before you plan to attend.
first_visit_tips: Ask whether the online community is still active
Ask whether any support sessions or events are scheduled
Ask what Celebrating You costs, since the site does not say

records.notes: The newest dated item is a post from July 26, 2017, on the events page. Footers read 2020 and are not counted. The social events page lists no dates. The contact page also lists widowsmitefoundationinc@gmail.com, which is not recorded. Registration for Celebrating You runs through an Eventbrite page, a lead platform, so no facts were taken from it.

records.name: Workers Revolutionary Collective
records.summary: A nonprofit cooperative of member-run collectives in Philadelphia that does mutual aid. Its collectives cover food and land work, health and addiction care, a laundry for people without stable housing, a car-share network, art, and worker education and media.
records.what_you_do: Choose the collective that fits your skills, such as land and food work, media and economic education, art, the laundry, or health and addiction care. Then say which one you want on the Worker Introduction form, or on the contact form under the Joining WRC topic.

cost.text: No dues or fees are mentioned; donations are welcome

first_step.how: Fill out the Worker Introduction form on wrc.life, or use the contact form and choose the Joining WRC topic, then name the collective that interests you.
first_step.basis: The site has a public introduction form and a Joining WRC topic on its contact form, and the FAQ asks for volunteers for each collective. It does not describe meetings or an orientation.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first meeting or an orientation, so a first visit is not defined. Each collective runs its own projects, such as a laundry, food and land work, media, or art, so the first step is picking one and asking what it needs. Ask each collective how and where it meets.
first_visit_tips: Pick one collective before you reach out, since each has its own work
Use the Joining WRC topic on the contact form
Ask how and where the collective meets, since the site does not say

records.notes: The FAQ calls the group nonpartisan and describes its work as educating about class struggle and organizing nonviolent community action. The owner may want to check that against the scope rule. The PHL Laundry and helpfuljellyfish collectives are part of this group, so they are not listed as leads. The contact page has no phone or street address. The contact form's webmaster@wrc.life address is for website problems only. Donation handles were left out.

records.name: Community Schools @George Washington High School
records.summary: George Washington High School is one of the City's Community Schools. Volunteers help with after school and family programs, and open shifts are posted on the City's volunteer portal.
records.what_you_do: Help students get groceries, tend the school's community garden, or support after school and family programs. Clearances are required before you start.

first_step.how: Call the school at (215) 400-3100 and ask for a community school coordinator, then ask which volunteer roles are open right now.
first_step.basis: Volunteers must complete school and city clearances before they start, and the way in runs through the coordinators.
first_step.what_to_expect: Before any shift, you finish a packet of school and city paperwork that includes Pennsylvania child abuse history and criminal background checks. Volunteers support after school and family programs, along with student access to groceries and the garden. Shift times and length are not on the pages we could read, so ask the coordinators.
first_visit_tips: Ask which role needs help before you start the paperwork
Gather the documents for each check, since the packet lists several
Ask what days and hours the shifts run, since the pages do not say

records.notes: The Galaxy volunteer portal returned HTTP 403 on this pass and was not retried. Its clearance list, active status, 2026-10 sign of life and portal contact are carried over from tier 1 and were not re-read. The City page lists the school phone and two community school coordinators (Jessica Carvin and Lilibeth Castillo) with their own emails and phone numbers. They differ from the portal contact, so they are not recorded as contact_name. The City page shows only 2023 news posts and no volunteer listings. District volunteer pages (philasd.org/face/volunteer, philasd.org/face/contact-us/volunteer-support/ and the 2024 volunteering FAQ) returned 404, so the District packet was not verified.

notes: Seven groups, each given up to six fetches. Fetches used: 31, including 404 and 403 responses. Searches used: 1 of 1, restricted to phila.gov and philasd.org. Status changes from tier 1: There's Hope, Wesley Proctor Ministries and Widow's Mite Foundation move to dormant, since their newest dated evidence is from April 2024, April 2020 and July 2017. They are still published with dormant status, so the owner may want to decide how dormant groups should show. Surge Recovery, Transformation CDC and Workers Revolutionary Collective stay probably_active because their sites show no dated evidence. Several sub-pages returned 404 and are not counted as blocked.
